questions.question: Who was popularly known as the 'father of civil services in India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Cornwallis.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Cornwallis:-**

 
 
• **He is known as the "father of civil services in India" because he introduced the concept of a permanent civil service in India. Before him, civil servants were appointed on a temporary basis, and there was no clear career path for them.**
 
• Lord Cornwallis established the Civil Service Commission in 1786, which was responsible for recruiting and training civil servants. This commission laid the foundation for a professional and efficient civil service in India.
 
• Lord Cornwallis also introduced the concept of a hierarchy in the civil service, with different grades and ranks for different levels of responsibility. This helped to create a clear career path for civil servants and incentivized them to work harder.
 
• Lord Cornwallis's reforms were instrumental in creating a modern and efficient administrative system in India, which helped to lay the foundation for British rule in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William Bentinck:-**

 
 
• He was the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835.
 
• He is known for his social reforms, such as banning Sati and promoting Western education.
 
• However, he did not make any significant contributions to the civil service during his tenure.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie:-**
 
 
• He was the Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856.
 
• He is known for his ambitious infrastructure projects, such as building railways and telegraph lines. He also introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, which allowed the British to annex Indian states that did not have a male heir.
 
• However, he did not make any significant contributions to the civil service during his tenure.
 
 
 
• **John Shore:-**
 
 
• He was the Governor-General of India from 1793 to 1798.
 
• He is known for his administrative reforms, such as introducing the office of the Governor-General and creating a separate department for revenue.

questions.question: Which revolutionary organisation was established at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi in 1928?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the** **__**Hindustan Socialist Republican Association.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA):**

 
 
• Hindustan Republic Association at a historic meeting in the ruins of** Ferozshah Kotla in Delhi** was converted into Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in **September 1928.**
 
• Under the leadership of **Chandra Shekhar Azad**, the name of HRA was changed to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA).
 
• The participants included **Bhagat Singh**, Sukhdev, Bhagwaticharan Vohra from Punjab and Bejoy Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma, and Jaidev Kapur from the United Provinces.
 
• The HSRA decided to work under a collective leadership and adopted **socialism** as its official goal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Naujawan Sabha** was established in **1926** by revolutionary leaders like** Bhagat Singh** and **Sukhdev**.

 
 
• The organization aimed to awaken the **youth of India** against British colonial rule and instill revolutionary ideas, promoting socialism and the rights of workers.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Hindustan Republican Association/Army:**

 
 
• 
 
The **HRA** was founded in **October 1924** in **Kanpur** by** Ramprasad Bismil**, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee and Sachin Sanyal, with an aim to organise an armed revolution to overthrow the colonial government and establish in its place the Federal Republic of United States of India whose basic principle would be an adult franchise.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
The **Home Rule Society** was founded in **1916** by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak **and** Annie Besant.**

 
 
• 
 
**​**The primary objective of the society was to secure self-rule for India through constitutional means.

questions.question: On 31 October 1940, who among the following was arrested for offering individual Satyagraha to protest against India’s forced participation in Second World War?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was arrested on 31 October 1940 for offering individual Satyagraha to protest against India's forced participation in the Second World War.
 
• The individual Satyagraha was a non-violent protest initiated by Mahatma Gandhi to assert the right to free speech and oppose the British decision to make India a participant in the war without consulting Indian leaders.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was among the first batch of leaders to offer Satyagraha and face arrest.
 
• This movement highlighted the growing discontent among Indian leaders and the populace against British colonial rule and their unilateral decisions affecting India.
 
• The arrest of prominent leaders like Nehru drew significant attention to the Indian independence movement and the demand for self-governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Individual Satyagraha** was different from mass civil disobedience as it involved selected individuals who would openly defy the British laws and court arrest.
 
• The movement was part of the larger Indian independence struggle which included various phases like the Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru later became the first Prime Minister of independent India and played a crucial role in shaping the newly formed nation.
 
• Nehru's participation in the Satyagraha demonstrated his commitment to the principles of non-violence and self-rule advocated by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The arrest of leaders like Nehru and the subsequent events contributed to the mounting pressure on the British government to consider Indian demands for independence.

questions.question: Which Act opposed by Mahatma Gandhi in 1919 was a direct attack on the civil liberties and democratic rights of the Indian people?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rowlatt Act** was enacted in **1919 **by the British government to curb the growing nationalist upsurge in India.
 
• This Act authorized the government to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial for up to two years.
 
• It also allowed the government to search any place and arrest any person without a warrant.
 
• The Act was seen as a direct attack on the civil liberties and democratic rights of the Indian people, leading to widespread protests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahatma Gandhi strongly opposed the Rowlatt Act and initiated a nationwide protest against it, which is known as the **Rowlatt Satyagraha**.
 
• The protests against the Rowlatt Act led to the tragic event of the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** in April 1919.
 
• The Act was officially known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**.
 
• The widespread opposition to the Rowlatt Act marked a significant moment in India's struggle for independence.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement when in ________ a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**February 1922.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement was a major political protest in India that began in 1920 and lasted for two years.**
 
• The movement was led by **Mahatma Gandhi and was aimed at achieving independence from British rule.**
 
• The movement was successful in mobilizing a large number of people and in bringing about a number of changes, such as the repeal of the **Rowlatt Act.**
 
• However, the movement was also marked by violence, and in** February 1922, a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura, killing 22 policemen.**
 
• This incident led to Gandhi calling off the movement, as he believed that it had become violent and that it was no longer in the best interests of India.
 
• The **Chauri Chaura incident was a major setback for the Indian independence movement, but it also served as a reminder of the importance of non-violence.**
 
• **Gandhi's decision to call off the movement was a difficult one, but it was a decision that he believed was in the best interests of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• About Mahatma Gandhi:

• He died January 30, 1948, in Delhi, and the day is celebrated as Shaheed Diwas or Martyrs' Day.
 
 
 
• His autobiography is titled My Experiments with Truth.

questions.question: Qutub Minar is an example of _____ architecture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-Islamic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Qutub Minar (or Qutab Minar) is a minaret and "victory tower" that forms part of the Qutb complex.
 
• It is an example of Indo-Islamic architecture.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Mehrauli area of New Delhi, India.
 
• The height of Qutb Minar is 72.5 meters, making it the tallest minaret in the world built of bricks.
 
• The tower tapers, and has a 14.3 meters (47 feet) base diameter, reducing to 2.7 meters (9 feet) at the top of the peak. ​
 
• Between 1199 and 1503, Qutub-ud-Din Aibak and Shamsu'd-Din Iltutmish built a minar (minaret) near the southeast corner of the Quwwatu'l-Islam, drawing inspiration from their Ghurid homeland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Nagara or North Indian temple style

 
 
• Became popular in northern India.
 
• The entire temple is generally built on a stone platform with steps leading to it.
 
• No grand boundary walls or gateways (unlike the Dravida style).
 
• Earlier temples had one shikhara whereas later temples had many.
 
• The garbhagriha is located directly beneath the tallest shikhara.
 
 
 
• Dravidian Style of Architecture – South Indian Style
 
 
• The temple is enclosed within a compound wall.
 
• Gopuram: The entrance gateway in the centre of the front wall.
 
• Vimana: The shape of the main temple tower. It is a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically (unlike the Nagara style Shikhara that is curving).
 
• In the Dravida style, shikhara is the word used for the crowning element at the top of the temple (which is shaped like a stupika or octagonal cupola).
 
• At the entrance to the garbhagriha, there would be sculptures of fierce dvarapalas guarding the temple.
 
• Generally, there is a temple tank within the compound.
 
• Subsidiary shrines could be found wither within the main tower or beside the main tower.
 
• Example in the Sriranganathar Temple at Srirangam, Tiruchirappalli, there are 7 concentric rectangular enclosure walls each having gopurams. The tower in the centre has the garbhagriha.
 
• Famous temple towns of Tamil Nadu: Kanchipuram, Thanjavur (Tanjore), Madurai and Kumbakonam.
 
• In the 8th to 12th centuries – temples were not confined to being religious centres but became administrative centres as well with large swathes of land.
 
 
 
• The Vesara Style is a hybrid temple architecture. It has features of both the Nagara and Dravidian style of temple architecture.
 
 
• In particular, the shape of the superstructure over the sanctum is usually pyramidal in profile, and shorter than the northern shikhara tower.
 
• In plan, the walls and superstructure are broadly circular, or a straight-sided cone, though its geometry is based on rotating a square imposed on a circle.

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an understanding between the Indian National Congress and the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim League.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an understanding between the Congress and the Muslim League.
 
• Congress and the Muslim League decided to work together for **representative government in the country** through the Lucknow pact.
 
• As a result of the Lucknow Pact, congress accepted **separate electorates.**
 
• This was the first time both the INC and the Muslim League's leaders had met in a joint session.
 
• The pact provided a joint political platform for the** Moderates, Extremists, and the Muslim League.​**
 
• The Indian National Congress was headed by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** and the All-India Muslim League was led by **Muhammad Ali Jinnah.**
 
• Lucknow Pact was adopted by Congress at its Lucknow session on **29 December 1916.**

questions.question: ______ is an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that partitioned British India into two new independent dominions of India and Pakistan in 1947.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Independence Act of 1947** partitioned British India into two separate dominions, **India and Pakistan, based on religious lines.**
 
• The act facilitated the transfer of power from British colonial rule to the newly formed governments of **India and Pakistan.**
 
• It granted full **legislative authority to India and Pakistan**, establishing them as independent and sovereign nations.
 
• The partition resulted in widespread communal violence and riots between religious communities, leading to a significant loss of life and displacement of people.
 
• The act allowed princely states to choose between joining India, joining Pakistan, or remaining independent, leaving the decision to the rulers of these states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Rowlatt Act**, also known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary** Crimes Act of 1919,** was a legislative act passed by the British colonial government in India during the period of British rule.

 
 
• It was named after its sponsor,** Sir Sidney Rowlatt,** who was a British judge.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act** refers to several legislative acts passed by the** British Parliament** during the period of **British rule in India.**
 
 
• These acts were intended to regulate and govern the administration of **British India.**
 
 
 
• **​Pitt's India Act, **officially known as the** East India Company Act 1784**, was an important piece of legislation passed by the **British Parliament under the leadership of Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.**
 
 
• The act was designed to bring about significant reforms in the governance and administration of the British East India Company's territories in India.

__
 
• **In 1929, under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Lahore Congress formalized the demand of Purna Swaraj.**
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was a prominent leader of the **Indian National Congress and later became the first Prime Minister of independent India.**
 
• **The Lahore Congress session held on December 31, 1929,** marked a significant milestone in India's struggle for independence as it declared the goal of complete self-rule or Purna Swaraj for India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He was born on** October 31, 1875, in Nadiad, Gujarat,** and passed away on December 15, 1950.
 
• **Vallabhbhai Patel **played a crucial role in India's struggle for independence from British rule.
 
• He was a close associate of **Mahatma Gandhi** and actively participated in various civil disobedience movements led by the Indian National Congress.
 
• As the leader of the** Bardoli Satyagraha in 1928**, he successfully led a farmers' protest against oppressive land taxes imposed by the British colonial authorities.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi, born Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat, India, was a preeminent leader of India's independence movement against British rule.**
 
 
• He is widely known as Mahatma, a term meaning "great soul," and is revered as the Father of the Nation in India.
 
• Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolence, called Satyagraha, became a guiding principle for the Indian freedom struggle and inspired civil rights movements around the world.
 
 
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose, also known as Netaji, was a prominent nationalist leader and freedom fighter in India's struggle for independence from British rule.**
 
 
• He was born on **January 23, 1897, in Cuttack, Odisha, India,** and his untimely death occurred on **August 18, 1945.**
 
• Subhas Chandra Bose played a significant role in mobilizing the Indian masses against British colonial rule.
 
• He advocated for complete independence and believed in taking more assertive and militant measures to achieve it.
 
• Bose was a charismatic leader and an influential orator who captured the imagination of many Indians.

questions.question: In his ‘Drain of Wealth’ argument, who among the following stated that Britain was completely draining India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was an Indian political leader, educator, and an early Indian nationalist who is credited with the 'Drain of Wealth' theory.
 
• In his book, **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'**, Naoroji argued that a significant portion of India's wealth was being drained to Britain, causing widespread poverty in India.
 
• His theory highlighted the economic exploitation of India under British rule and became a key point of criticism against colonial policies.
 
• Naoroji's efforts were instrumental in raising awareness about the economic impact of British colonialism on India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was also known as the 'Grand Old Man of India' and was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the British Parliament, where he advocated for Indian self-rule and economic reforms.
 
• His work laid the foundation for subsequent economic theories and nationalist movements in India.
 
• Naoroji's contributions were crucial in shaping the early phase of the Indian independence struggle.
